courses.title: Applied Linear and Nonlinear Control
courses.text: A postgraduate course linking advanced control theory to robots, with MATLAB, Simulink, ROS 2 and motion-capture experiments. It covers linear and nonlinear dynamics, stability theory, optimal control and safety-critical control, and ends with controllers running on mobile robots and manipulators.
topics: MATLAB live scripts and the inverted pendulum
State feedback: pole placement and LQR
courses.link_label: Lab code and live scripts on GitHub

courses.title: Formal Analysis and Control of Autonomous Systems
courses.text: The formal side of autonomy: modelling systems so they can be reasoned about, stating requirements precisely in temporal logic, verifying them, and synthesising controllers that meet them by construction. Lab sessions turn these ideas into working code.

items: Real-time spatiotemporal tubes for dynamic unsafe sets
Reinforcement learning for STL with funnels

highlights.title: Motion-capture arena
highlights.text: A PhaseSpace system tracks robots in real time, so every controller is tested against ground truth. Our ROS driver is open source.

highlights.title: F1TENTH racing
highlights.text: Students build and race a 1:10-scale autonomous car, and the full software stack is on GitHub.

highlights.title: Taught with MathWorks
highlights.text: CP 241 is a MathWorks–IISc collaboration, and every lab runs on real robots, not only in simulation.

highlights.title: Award-winning work
highlights.text: Best Paper at the Indian Control Conference 2024, the Prof. Satish Dhawan Award, and Best Presentation at the IISc EECS Symposium 2023.

highlights.title: Experiments on video
